newsitem.title: POLAND: Sokolow mulls strategic investor - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sokolow mulls strategic investor - paper.

text.p: Polish meat processing firm Sokolow SA is considering selling shares to a strategic investor, the company's president told the financial daily Parkiet on Thursday.
"The possession of an investor with whom the firm could form a long-term strategy, including the planning of capital investments, is necessary," Parkiet quoted Jan Augustynowicz as saying.
Augustynowicz also said Sokolow's ownership structure was too dispersed, with only a BIG subsidiary holding more than five percent of shares. @
Sokolow has said it hoped to lift its market share to 15 percent from six percent in three years in part by buying other meat-processing companies.
Augustynowicz also told Parkiet a share or bond issue was possible in 1997.
He said Sokolow would likely net 7.5 million zlotys in 1996 on an operating profit of 12.5 million zlotys and sales of 240 million zloyts. @
In 1995 it earned 5.4 million zlotys on an operating profit of 5.7 million zlotys and sales of 175.4 million zlotys.
